skills.observableOutcome: Predict and observe whether familiar objects float or sink.
Compare liquid properties, capacity, dissolving and mixing.
Identify heat sources and choose safe actions.

activities.prompt: Which familiar object is most likely to float on water?

optionRationales.a: A dry leaf usually floats.
optionRationales.b: A metal coin usually sinks.
optionRationales.c: A small stone usually sinks.

activities.feedbackCorrect: Well done! You chose the best answer.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: Nice try. Think about what you have learned, then try again.

activities.prompt: What would a wooden block usually do when gently placed on water?

optionRationales.a: A wooden block usually floats.
optionRationales.b: Wood does not dissolve just because it is placed in water.
optionRationales.c: The block remains a solid.

activities.feedbackCorrect: Well done! You chose the best answer.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: Nice try. Think about what you have learned, then try again.

activities.prompt: Which object is most likely to sink?

optionRationales.a: Cork usually floats.
optionRationales.b: A metal spoon usually sinks.
optionRationales.c: A dry leaf usually floats.

activities.feedbackCorrect: Well done! You chose the best answer.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: Nice try. Think about what you have learned, then try again.

activities.prompt: How can you find out whether a safe classroom object floats?

options.text: Place it gently in water and observe

optionRationales.a: A careful water test gives observable evidence.
optionRationales.b: Colour does not tell whether an object floats.
optionRationales.c: Objects must never be tasted as a test.

activities.safetyNote: Use adult-approved objects and room-temperature water.
activities.feedbackCorrect: Well done! You chose the best answer.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: Nice try. Think about what you have learned, then try again.

activities.prompt: A wide toy boat floats. What helps it stay on the water?

options.text: Its shape helps it push water aside

optionRationales.a: A boat's shape helps it push aside water and stay afloat.
optionRationales.b: A boat still has weight.
optionRationales.c: A boat is not made of water.

activities.feedbackCorrect: Well done! You chose the best answer.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: Nice try. Think about what you have learned, then try again.

activities.prompt: What shape does water take when poured into a cup?

optionRationales.a: A liquid takes the shape of its container.
optionRationales.b: A wooden block does not set the water's shape.
optionRationales.c: Water changes shape when poured into another container.

activities.feedbackCorrect: Well done! You chose the best answer.

optionRationales.b: If none is added or spilled, the amount stays the same.

activities.prompt: What happens when salt is stirred into water?

options.text: It dissolves and spreads through the water
It floats forever as a lump

optionRationales.a: Salt dissolves in water and spreads through it.
optionRationales.b: Salt does not turn into a stone.
optionRationales.c: Most salt grains are no longer visible after dissolving.

activities.feedbackCorrect: Well done! You chose the best answer.
activities.feedbackIncorrect: Nice try. Think about what you have learned, then try again.

activities.prompt: Which material does not dissolve easily in water?

optionRationales.a: Sand does not dissolve in water.
optionRationales.b: Sugar dissolves in water.

optionRationales.a: Dissolved sugar remains in the solution.
optionRationales.b: Dissolving does not destroy sugar.
optionRationales.c: Sugar does not turn water into oil.

optionRationales.a: Oil and water usually form separate layers.

optionRationales.c: Sand does not help sugar dissolve.

activities.prompt: A cooking pot is on a hot stove. What should a child do?

options.text: Touch the pot to test it
Stay away and tell an adult

optionRationales.a: Staying away and telling an adult is safe.
optionRationales.b: Touching a hot pot can cause a burn.
optionRationales.c: A child should not move a hot pot.

activities.safetyNote: Never touch a hot stove, pot or flame.
